en.title: Bethesda Confirms Fallout 3 & New Vegas Remasters, Fallout 5 in Pre-Production
en.summary: The studio behind the iconic Wasteland revealed its long-term plans, including highly anticipated remasters of beloved classics and the early stages of its next mainline Fallout entry. Fans can rejoice as their favorite post-apocalyptic worlds are set to be revisited with modern touches.
en.body:
Bethesda Game Studios has officially pulled back the curtain on its ambitious multi-year roadmap, confirming what many fans have long hoped for: remasters of both **Fallout 3** and **Fallout: New Vegas** are officially in the works. This announcement comes as part of a broader strategy to refocus on core franchises, with **The Elder Scrolls VI** remaining the studio's primary long-term development goal. The news also includes the exciting, albeit early, confirmation that **Fallout 5** is currently in pre-production, signaling a significant future for the series.

This move to remaster **Fallout 3** and **Fallout: New Vegas** is a strategic play that acknowledges the enduring popularity of these titles. **Fallout 3**, released in 2008, redefined the open-world RPG for a generation with its atmospheric setting and engaging gameplay. Its 2010 follow-up, **Fallout: New Vegas**, developed by Obsidian Entertainment, is often lauded for its complex narrative, player choice, and deep RPG mechanics, garnering a dedicated cult following. Bringing these games back with updated visuals and potentially modern gameplay enhancements for current platforms is a welcome prospect for both long-time fans and newcomers eager to experience these seminal entries.

## A Return to Beloved Wastelands

The announcement of remasters for **Fallout 3** and **Fallout: New Vegas** has ignited passionate discussions across the gaming community. For many, these titles represent pivotal moments in the franchise's history, offering vastly different yet equally compelling visions of the post-nuclear American landscape. **Fallout 3** provided the initial leap into a fully realized 3D Wasteland, while **New Vegas** delved deeper into the political machinations and moral ambiguities of survival. The prospect of experiencing these worlds with updated graphics, smoother performance, and possibly even quality-of-life improvements is incredibly exciting. This also raises hopes for potential enhancements to gameplay mechanics, making them more accessible to a modern audience while retaining the core experiences that made them classics.

## What's Next for the Franchise

While specific release dates for the **Fallout 3** and **Fallout: New Vegas** remasters have not yet been announced, their confirmation is a major step. Bethesda has also stated its continued commitment to supporting **Starfield** and is diligently working on **The Elder Scrolls VI**. The pre-production status of **Fallout 5** suggests it is still many years away, with the remasters and **The Elder Scrolls VI** likely taking priority. Fans will be eagerly awaiting further details on these projects, especially any information regarding which studio might be handling the **New Vegas** remaster, given Obsidian's original involvement.

content_raw: They've pulled back the curtain on their multi-year plans. Out of nowhere, Bethesda Game Studios has suddenly revealed a roadmap of its plans for the next few years ahead, including multiple Fallout games, continued work on The Elder Scrolls VI, and an intent to keep supporting Starfield. The biggest news here concerns Fallout, with Fallout 3 Remastered and Fallout: New Vegas Remastered both officially confirmed.
